Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: What would be Lok Sabha 2024 results if BJD, BSP, JD(S) & JJP would have also joined India Alliance?
Answer: Of the four parties mentioned BSP and JJP do not have any representative. Their joining is of no use. BJD has one MP and JDS is already a part of NDA. If BSP were to have been a part of NDA, BJP may have to concede at least ten seats. Also BJP may have increased its vote share by another 6% throughout UP which would have got 50+ seat for itself and another 8 to 10 for BSP. If JJP has been a part of pre-poll understanding, BJP would not have lost five seat. But BJP may have to have ceded three seats. Also NDA could have retained all the ten seats. BJD not being a part of NDA, helped BJP to sweep 20 out of 21 seats. Hence BJD not to be an ally of BJP helped NDA. If BJP and BSP were to have been part of NDA BJP might have increased its number to 262+ and NDA by 336+.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Will the BJP come to power again after Modiji?
Answer: Bharatiya Janata Party has been going strength to strength after every election. BJP is either ruling or in coalition with other parties in 23 states out of 28. When the party is in control of such a vast tract of land, doubting BJP to come to power in future is a futile exercise. BJP might have lost 63 seats in 2024, but won two new mid-sized states of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.. Also BJP won Arunachal Pradesh. and BJP’s alliance partner won Sikkim. The doubt expressed in the question is because of the sudden drop in numbers in 2024. It is a common phenomena which happens election after election. BJP’s grip over the politics of the nation is strong and firm. BJP also has a galaxy of leaders who are ready to take any responsibility. For another twenty to thirty years BJP will continue to rule the nation. Also the opposition is divided, no common agenda or common ideology. The hosh potch alliance without common goal or ideology will not help the opposition any. Also they do not have unity. Hence this opposition replacing BJP or NDA seems impossible for some time to come.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: How important is it for the AAP to promote a leader from the Dalit community to lead the party in Punjab, considering the demographics and electoral dynamics of the state?
Answer: It is not a dalit community leader to lead AAP in Punjab, but a pragmatic approach to the Khalistani issues. AAP leaders are in cohorts with Khalistanis and have also accepted funds from them. This have angered an important segment of the population, because of which AAP is surging down. AAP could win only three seats out of thirteen even though they have their Government in place in Punjab. The ideology of AAP of pleasing the Khalistanis only will backfire on them. Congress did projected a dalit leader to CM. But Congress lost election humiliatingly. Hence dalit candidate is not the issue. The issue is good governance and keeping distance from the separatists. Kejriwal having taken illegal money from Khalistanis cannot remain balanced in his approach to the issue of Khalistan. Hence the electoral dynamics too will remain uncertain for AAP.

Name: Rajagopalan K Suryanarayan
Question: Is it true that the AAP is not participating in the upcoming assembly elections? What is your opinion on their decision?
Answer: Whether AAP is participating in the upcoming assembly elections or Delhi assembly elections rests on the verdict in the case of Delhi Excise Policy Scam. In the Excise Policy Scam ED has filed chargesheets where AAP as a party as an accused. What the final verdict of the court is unknown, but the possibility of AAP being derecognised cannot be set aside. Hence AAP may be forced to not participate in the elections. But the AAP itself do not intend to not participate in the assembly elections.
